## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Earth’s Water

GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As the pair approaches a larger mass concentration, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite.

The changing distance between the satellites is a measurement scientists use to infer shifts in mass. It is not a direct measurement of groundwater; the inferred mass changes can help reveal water movement on Earth.

These changes include shifts in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, as well as sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
